items.title: Pantone chip product swap
items.description: A heap of heart-shaped churros sits on a Pantone-style swatch card with its own colour code. Any food or product brand can name a 'shade' after its hero item.

items.title: Doodle over product shot
items.description: A real cookie becomes a fresh-from-the-oven tray held by drawn oven mitts, with a sketched mouse eyeing it. Cheap to make and easy to repeat with any product.

items.title: Bracket annotation relatable joke
items.description: Brackets split a tub of ice cream into stages from 'just one bite' to 'might as well finish it'. The product shot doubles as a relatable joke about overindulging.

items.title: Claw machine product grab
items.description: A 3D claw machine plucks one pack from a pile of flavours. Works as a 'pick your favourite' or giveaway visual for any range of packaged products.

items.title: Weekday deals loading
items.description: A loading bar fills up with products slide by slide, so people swipe to see it hit 100%. Swap in this week's specials or a snack bundle and let the full bar be the deal.
media: Always on/Carousel/Weekday deals loading /Weekday loading with some snacks_.jpeg

items.title: Forgot an ingredient panic
items.description: She finishes baking, spots the baking powder still on the counter and freezes. A relatable kitchen fail that any food or grocery brand can recreate with its own product as the punchline.

items.title: Manager's voice note orders
items.description: Staff act out a voice note from their absent manager, with the 'strict instructions' turning into a team ice cream break. Easy staff-led format for any store or restaurant.

items.title: Knife through the paper reveal
items.description: A blade slices through a red paper backdrop and a hand pushes through with the message written on the palm. Cheap, punchy way to drop a single line or launch.

items.title: Lift doors open on the menu
items.description: Lift doors open to reveal chefs and crates of fresh produce, then close on the restaurant logo and launch date. A neat teaser structure for openings and new menus.

items.title: Dinner plans gone wrong
items.description: A short film where a cooking attempt ends in the sink and family saves the night with home food. Story-led ad that lands on warmth instead of product features.

items.path: Always on/Reels/Aesthetic/Let me wipe the camera.mp4
items.title: Wipe-the-lens food reveal
items.description: 'Wait, let me wipe the camera', a hand wipes the lens and an empty table is suddenly full of food. Simple in-camera transition that works for any menu or product spread.
media: Always on/Reels/Aesthetic/Let me wipe the camera.mp4

items.title: The job title grip
items.description: An arm holds out a handful of everyday items that sum up a 'social media manager grip'. Swap in any role, customer type or product range for a quick relatable post.

items.title: Same bag, different places
items.description: One branded bag sits locked off in a gym, park and court while life moves around it. Shows a product fits every part of the day without saying it.

items.title: Making a video from the boss's voice note
items.description: Staff play the manager's voice note and literally act out every instruction. Low-effort, staff-led content that shows team personality.

items.title: Boss wanted a video, I took photos
items.description: Stills of an event setup get dragged around with editor handles to fake motion. Self-aware joke that turns leftover photos into usable content.

items.title: Water spill hidden message
items.description: Water poured on a surface makes a hidden message appear on paper. A tactile visual hook any brand can use to deliver one line.

items.title: Phone screen pull-out
items.description: A finger pinches the drink on a phone screen and the real product appears on the table above it. Clean product intro with name and flavour notes.

items.title: Hands clear the table
items.description: Plates are named one by one, then hands grab everything at once and the table is empty. Quick menu roundup with a fun ending.

items.title: Yes, but... trend
items.description: Each slide splits into a dreamy "yes" photo on top and the messy reality "but" underneath, like a cake and then the pile of dishes. Brands can play the honest flip side of their category for an easy relatable laugh.

items.title: Everything for the week
items.description: A photo dump of creators in branded merch, mixed with short cut-out video edits where the product and gear float around them. Works for any brand drop or activation recap that needs to feel fun and creator-made.

items.title: Shopping basket service menu
items.description: A pink shopping basket holds a phone, camera and props that stand in for what a social media manager offers. Turns a service list into a shoppable flat-lay.

items.title: Me vs you drink heads
items.description: Two people at a cafe have their heads swapped for top-down shots of an iced matcha and an iced latte, labelled 'me' and 'you'. A quick way to tag-a-friend with any two menu items.

items.title: Before and after coffee meme
items.description: Side-by-side photos of a screaming dog and a calm one, captioned 'me before coffee' and 'me after coffee'. A classic two-panel meme any cafe or energy brand can redo with its own product.

items.title: Food origin quiz story
items.description: A 9GAG story asks where Swedish meatballs come from, using a multiple-choice quiz sticker over the dish. Food trivia gets quick taps and works for any brand with a story behind its product.

items.title: Topping poll story
items.description: Quaker surrounds a 'how do you top it?' poll with four rice cakes, each with a different topping. Shows the product's range while getting the audience to vote.

items.title: Monthly reads cafe flat-lay
items.description: A top-down cafe table shot with a book cover dropped in the middle and 'What I read in August' text. An easy monthly series for book, cafe or lifestyle accounts.

items.title: Process to product split
items.description: A close-up of frothing coffee sits above a clean, minimal shot of the finished iced coffee. Shows how it's made versus what you get, with no copy needed.

items.title: Fake post breaking the frame
items.description: Chupa Chups pours lollipops out of a giant tub, through a fake Instagram post UI and into a mouth below. The post plays with the feed itself, which makes people stop scrolling.

items.title: Search bar USP list
items.description: A search bar types 'what makes our cookies special?' with autocomplete answers listing the selling points. A light way to share product benefits without a hard-sell layout.

items.title: Folders and DM services post
items.description: Desktop folder icons float around a person reading a newspaper, each one named after a service, plus a DM bubble asking what's offered. Turns a services list into a scene.

items.title: Hand-drawn book annotations
items.description: A hand holds a novel against a warm backdrop with handwritten notes and arrows pointing out the setting, vibe and rating. Works for any product that has 'features' worth labelling.

items.title: Notes app to-do list
items.description: An iPhone Notes-style weekend to-do list slips the brand's serum and moisturiser in between brunch and beach plans. Product placement that reads like a personal note.

items.title: Numbered bubble quiz story
items.description: Four numbered circles show different breakfast options, linked to a quiz sticker asking which is your ideal. A simple vote format any menu or range can reuse.

items.title: Eye test colour joke
items.description: A red-tinted iced drink sits under an 'Eye test' headline: see yellow you're fine, see red you need coffee. A one-joke static that's easy to adapt to any product colour.

items.title: Emoji slider menu picker
items.description: A stack of burgers sits next to a story emoji slider, inviting people to slide to their pick. Uses a native story feature to get taps on menu items.

items.title: Flowchart where product wins
items.description: A yes/no flowchart about solving problems loops every answer back to a glass of chai. A tongue-in-cheek format where all roads lead to your product.

items.title: Ingredients pie chart
items.description: A cookie is cut like a pie chart, with the missing slices replaced by lemon, poppy seeds and an old recipe card. Shows what goes into a product in one clean visual.

items.title: Highlighted text quote post
items.description: A quote is shown as selected iPhone text, complete with the Copy / Select All / Share menu, over a calm lifestyle photo. Makes a quote feel like something worth saving and sharing.

items.title: Emoji slider story template
items.description: A template with a vertical strip of food photos next to an emoji slider. Drop in your own menu or range and let people slide to their favourite.

items.title: Pantone product range swatches
items.description: Six different croissants line up on Pantone chips, each matched to its own named shade. A neat way to show off a full range or flavour lineup.

items.title: Half-and-half split scene
items.description: One frame is split down the middle: a book in bed on one side, iced coffee on a table on the other, lined up so they read as one object. Handwritten labels tie the two moments together.

items.title: Four-dish menu quiz story
items.description: A restaurant shows four breakfast plates around a numbered quiz sticker asking which one you'd choose. Gets votes and shows off the menu in one story.

items.title: Tear-off flyer tabs
items.description: A street-flyer mockup with tear-off tabs offering romance tropes, one already pulled off. Works for any brand with a list of options, flavours or perks to 'take'.

items.title: Maps route travel diary
items.description: A rainy windscreen shot gets a Google Maps route overlaid on the glass and 'back home' text. A diary-style format for travel, road trip or delivery brands.

items.title: Phone widget day planner
items.description: A cosy home scene is layered with a music player, a clock and a Notes checklist titled 'day plans'. A day-in-the-life story that feels personal and easy to copy.

items.title: Chalk text top-down table
items.description: Shot from directly above, a person reads at a round table with 'my favourite books of 2025' written around the edge in chalk-style type. A year-end favourites post with a strong layout.

items.title: Annotated intro portrait
items.description: A designer stands in a doorway with a cutout outline, a big 'Hi, I'm Laura!' and arrows pointing to quick facts. Ideal for team intros, founder posts or a new ambassador.

items.title: Pantone drinks lineup
items.description: Three iced drinks shot from above sit on Pantone chips that match their colour. Clean and simple, and it works for any drinks menu or flavour range.

items.title: Text field plans flat-lay
items.description: Cutout products float over an unmade bed around a selected iMessage text field reading 'my plans for the weekend'. Turns a product bundle into a relatable weekend plan.

items.title: Office voice note series
items.description: 'Lebo, quick one, Episode 2' plays a long voice note while she reacts at her desk. Episodic, local-feeling office comedy a brand can run as a recurring series.

items.title: This or that coffee pick
items.description: Black coffee at the top, a latte at the bottom, with 'this or that' in between. A simple two-option choice that pulls comments, easy to repeat with any pair of products.

items.title: Pause to choose pairing
items.description: Mid-scroll frame of a 'pause to choose your pairing' reel, with wine and snack packs flicking past in two windows. Viewers try to pause on a combo, which keeps them watching.

items.title: Pause game shuffle frame
items.description: Another mid-shuffle frame from the pause-to-choose pairing reel, showing how the product images scroll fast in each window. Useful as a reference for the motion and pacing.

items.path: Always on/Reels/Pause to choose/Pause to choose your pairing.png
items.title: Pause to choose result
items.description: The landed frame of the pause game: a rosé paired with a dill pickle almond snack. Shows how each pause gives a clear product combo people can comment about.
media: Always on/Reels/Pause to choose/Pause to choose your pairing.png

items.title: Bag-cam unboxing
items.description: Shot from inside a gift bag looking up at the sky as hands pull out a 'Coming soon' card. Fresh POV angle for launches and teasers.

items.title: Wes Anderson day in the life
items.description: Pastel, symmetrical shots with narrated captions follow a character through her day. Borrow the film style for a branded day in the life.

items.title: Caught on camera, budget joke
items.description: A creator catches a guy staring, then cuts to a caption about still being in your budget. Hook-first skit with a sales twist at the end.

items.title: Coffee and a song
items.description: Top-down iced coffee with a music player overlay and big serif lyrics. Calm, moody format pairing a product with a track.

items.title: Split-panel mood edit
items.description: Multiple framed panels play at once as she listens, scrolls and snacks. Film-look grid layout that makes a simple moment feel editorial.

items.title: Giant everyday objects
items.description: A creator holds an oversized ice cream and stands next to a giant pigeon in the street. Big-scale CGI that turns a product into a scroll stopper.

items.title: Brick catch match cut
items.description: Hands toss a brick across guide lines and match cut into a wall being built. Smooth handover edit for building, trade or process stories.

items.title: App-switcher scroll edit
items.description: The video moves through the phone's app switcher, landing on a food shot and a hypnotic spiral. Native phone UI framing that feels like the viewer's own screen.

items.title: You're this close
items.description: Opens on a pinching hand with "You're this close to..." then zooms in slide by slide until the tiny text between the fingers is readable. Good for any brand line you want people to physically lean in for.

items.title: Slide to open
items.description: Cupped hands hide something with "Guess what's hiding behind these hands?" and the swipe opens them to reveal the product. Any pack shot or new launch can sit behind the hands.

items.title: Hobby ideas, scrapbook style
items.description: Each slide is one activity idea (reading, sketch, picnic) with a big pink word, a one-line tip and polaroid inserts. A brand can turn it into weekend or occasion ideas with their product sitting in the scene.

items.title: Seamless monthly recap
items.description: One long panorama sliced into slides, with shapes and photos crossing the cuts so every swipe flows into the next. Good template for a monthly recap or wins post told as one continuous strip.

items.title: Recharge my battery
items.description: "Time to recharge my battery" sits over an empty battery that fills up with travel items one at a time. Fill it with whatever your audience needs to recharge, like snacks, a holiday or the product.

items.title: Open this envelope
items.description: A red envelope shows a new pun-filled note on every slide ("Client Crush", "Be Our Clientine") before the logo signs off. Easy Valentine's or occasion post for any brand with a few good wordplay lines.

items.title: Keep scrolling sandwich
items.description: "Keep scrolling" sits next to the edge of a slice of bread, and the sandwich keeps going across every slide. Any long product (a sub, a sausage, a scarf) can stretch the carousel for a silly payoff.

items.title: Pick a number
items.description: "If you're looking for a sign, pick a number" with numbered lines that run across the slides, each one leading to a different product and the need it solves. Good for brands with a range people struggle to choose from.

items.title: Don't open this
items.description: Torn-paper slides keep warning people to stop ("This is your last warning", "Still here? Wow.") until the reveal lands on the product. Reverse psychology works for any launch or new range drop.

items.title: Timestamped day in my life
items.description: A cover promises a timestamped day as a graphic designer, then each slide is a candid moment with a clock time and a casual caption. Brands can hand this to staff or creators to show the people behind the work.

items.title: Photo dump in the share sheet
items.description: An outfit shoot unfolds through desktop folders and an iOS share sheet of selected photos. Fun way to package a photo carousel as a reel.

items.title: Calendar day planner
items.description: A calendar widget plays each time slot as a mini video player. Turns a day in the life into a schedule viewers can follow.

items.title: Sponsor collage day out
items.description: A creator moves through Roland Garros in a split collage with Perrier cans and bottles popping in. Event plus product placement edit with lots of layers.

items.title: Temperature countdown drink
items.description: Degree counters drop from +35 to +21 as she sips the iced drink. Simple visual for showing how refreshing a product is.

items.title: Day of the week outfits
items.description: Split screens show a new outfit and treat for each day, with a top-down legs-up shot alongside. Repeatable weekly format for fashion or snack brands.

items.title: Desktop window menu tour
items.description: A pop-up window frames each dish while a cursor clicks for the menu description. Desktop UI framing that explains food without a voiceover.

items.title: Car rush transition hook
items.description: She sets down a chair in the road, a car flies past and she is suddenly seated talking to camera. A jolt in the first seconds that earns the talking head.

items.title: Fill-in-the-silhouettes flat lay
items.description: Blue silhouettes fill one by one with real items to build a summer essentials kit. Clean way to show a product range or bundle.

items.title: Dancing asparagus price drop
items.description: Asparagus spears walk across a table past handwritten signs to land on the price. Cheap stop motion that turns a weekly special into something fun.

items.title: Shout for a free pizza
items.description: A billboard asks people to shout 'I love pizza' and a pizza is delivered to whoever does. Street stunt that films real reactions.

items.title: Street pickle tasting
items.description: A creator offers pickles from a jar to strangers on the street, POV style. Low-budget sampling that lets real people do the talking.

items.title: Shirt colour swap on a tree
items.description: A shirt hangs on a tree and props appear as the colourway keeps changing. Locked-off stop motion for showing range and colour options.

items.title: Above-the-head outfit tutorial
items.description: Step by step CapCut tutorial for the overhead phone-hold outfit shot. Teaches a trend, which makes it easy to save and share.

items.title: Summer kit silhouettes
items.description: Items pop in and out of blue silhouettes to build a summer packing list. Works for fashion or accessories showing a full kit.

items.title: Emoji recipe build
items.description: A cursor clicks each emoji and the drink builds layer by layer, ending on the logo. Playful drink or recipe reveal with zero words.

items.title: New burger walkout
items.description: A waitress walks out the door with the new burger and fries, with bold type naming each item. Simple launch format for a new menu item.

items.title: Hungry to full slider
items.description: A hand drags a dip lid between 'full' and 'hungry' and the table changes with it. Interactive-feeling joke for food brands with combos.

items.title: Doodle-to-dish table fill
items.description: Scribbled drawings appear on an empty table then turn into real dishes. Playful order build for cafes and restaurants.

items.title: Supermarket speed run
items.description: Fast POV dash through a store from cleaning machine to trolley to price signs. High-energy retail walkthrough for specials and store tours.

items.title: Signs you can't ignore
items.description: The product's shape shows up somewhere unexpected on every slide, a cloud, an ice cube, with the same line "the signs you can't ignore". Works for brands with an iconic shape or logo people will spot instantly.
